latin: Ideo angelus est obstinatus et inpenitens, quia subtracti sunt ei diuini impetus speciales.
translation: Therefore the angel is obstinate and unrepentant, because special divine impulses have been withdrawn from it.
translation_note: 'impetus speciales' ('special impulses') names the particular divine motions of the will whose withdrawal, on this account, fixes the fallen angel in its obstinacy; 'obstinatus et inpenitens' is the standard scholastic pairing for the fixed, unchangeable will of a fallen angel.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-swarm-batch6, from Latin at farmer1998:12689
doctrine: The thesis draws its conclusion ('ideo', therefore) from the immediately preceding 6.5 ('Angeli non fuerunt creati in gratia', farmer1998:12686). Farmer's note groups 6.5-6 together as 'again anti-Thomistic', citing Thomas, Summa Ia, q. 62 a. 3 and Ia, q. 64 a. 2 as the position opposed (paraphrase, farmer1998:12768). Edelheit states that 'Thesis 6 is directly connected to the previous thesis through the adverb "therefore" (ideo)' and glosses it: 'an angel is obstinate and impenitent since divine and special powers were taken from it' (edelheit2022:16567), connecting it to an earlier discussion of the possibility of removing grace from angels by God's absolute power (paraphrase, edelheit2022:16567).
context: Edelheit divides the eleven Giles theses into a first group, theses 1-7, on theological issues including angelology, and a second, theses 8-11, on natural philosophy (edelheit2022:15967). He reports that theses 5, 6 and 7 of this set 'are included in a recent English translation of selections from Pico's 900 Theses', in Copenhaver's *Magic and the Dignity of Man* (edelheit2022:16386); that translation is in copyright and is not reproduced here.
historiography: Edelheit calls thesis 6 'almost deduced' from thesis 5, noting that 'while thesis 5 opens the whole discussion of whether angels were created in grace, a complicated issue which cannot be reflected in a short thesis, thesis 6 brings into relief Pico's unique formulation' (edelheit2022:16988). He quotes the Latin of 6.6 verbatim (edelheit2022:16588).

quotations.text: Thesis 6 is directly connected to the previous thesis through the adverb ‘therefore’ (ideo).

not_established: Any reception of this thesis beyond Edelheit's chapter: not established by the sources consulted.
